clues: This city sits in the southwest of Virginia, in a valley in the Blue Ridge hills. It lies far to the southwest of Washington.
Heavy rain is the big weather risk here, and floods are the chief threat. When storms soak the hills, the water drains down into the town's one narrow valley.
In 1882 a big rail firm chose this small town as the place for its main office and its train shops. Two years later, the town had become a city.
The town market has sold goods in the open air for years without a break. It is the oldest market of its kind in the whole state.
A huge lit star glows on a mountain top in this city. Folks call the place the Star City of the South for it.
